{{Short description|Weighted tree representing s-t cuts of a graph}}

In [[combinatorial optimization]], the '''Gomory–Hu tree'''<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gomory | first1 = R. E. | author-link = Ralph E. Gomory | last2 = Hu | first2 = T. C. | author2-link = T. C. Hu | title = Multi-terminal network flows | journal = Journal of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics | volume = 9 | issue = 4| pages = 551–570 | year = 1961 | doi = 10.1137/0109047 }}</ref> of an [[undirected graph]] with capacities is a weighted [[Tree (graph theory)|tree]] that represents the minimum [[Cut (graph theory)|''s''-''t'' cuts]] for all ''s''-''t'' pairs in the graph. The Gomory–Hu tree can be constructed in {{math|{{abs|''V''}} − 1}} [[Maximum flow problem|maximum flow]] computations. It is named for [[Ralph E. Gomory]] and [[T. C. Hu]].

==Definition==
Let <math>G = (V_G, E_G, c)</math> be an undirected graph with <math>c(u,v)</math> being the capacity of the edge <math>(u,v)</math> respectively.

: Denote the minimum capacity of an {{mvar|s}}-{{mvar|t}} cut by <math>\lambda_{st}</math> for each <math> s, t \in V_G </math>.
: Let <math> T = (V_G, E_T) </math> be a tree, and denote the set of edges in an {{mvar|s}}-{{mvar|t}} path by <math>P_{st}</math> for each <math>s,t \in V_G</math>.
Then {{mvar|T}} is said to be a '''Gomory–Hu tree''' of {{mvar|G}}, if for each <math>s, t \in V_G</math>
: <math style="display">\lambda_{st} = \min_{e\in P_{st}} c(S_e, T_e),</math>
where
# <math>S_e, T_e \subseteq V_G</math> are the two connected components of <math>T \setminus \{e\}</math>, and thus <math>(S_e, T_e)</math> forms an {{mvar|s}}-{{mvar|t}} cut in {{mvar|G}}.
# <math>c(S_e, T_e)</math> is the capacity of the <math>(S_e,T_e)</math> cut in {{mvar|G}}.

==Algorithm==
'''Gomory–Hu Algorithm'''
:''Input'': A weighted undirected graph <math>G = ((V_G,E_G), c)</math>
: ''Output'': A Gomory–Hu Tree <math>T = (V_T, E_T).</math>
# Set <math>V_T = \{V_G\}, \ E_T = \empty.</math>
# Choose some <math>X \in V_T</math> with {{math|{{abs|''X''}} ≥ 2}} if such {{mvar|X}} exists. Otherwise, go to step 6.
# For each connected component <math>C = (V_C,E_C) \in T \setminus X,</math> let <math display=inline>S_C = \bigcup_{v_T \in V_C} v_T.</math> 
#:Let <math>
S = \{ S_C \mid C \text{ is a connected component in } T \setminus X \}.
</math> 
#: Contract the components to form <math>G' = ((V_{G'}, E_{G'}), c'),</math> where:<math display=block>
\begin{align}
  V_{G'} &= X \cup S \\[2pt]
  E_{G'} &= E_G|_{X \times X} \cup \{(u, S_C) \in X \times S \mid (u,v) \in E_G \text{ for some } v \in S_C \} \\[2pt]
  & \qquad \qquad \quad\! \cup \{(S_{C1}, S_{C2}) \in S \times S \mid (u,v) \in E_G \text{ for some } u \in S_{C1} \text{ and } v \in S_{C2} \} 
\end{align}</math>
#::<math>c':V_{G'} \times V_{G'} \to R^+</math> is the capacity function, defined as:<math display=block>
\begin{align}
  &\text{if }\ (u,S_C) \in E_G|_{X \times S}: &&c'(u,S_C) = \!\!\! \sum_{\begin{smallmatrix} v \in S_C : \\ (u,v) \in E_G \end{smallmatrix}} \!\!\! c(u,v) \\[4pt]
  &\text{if }\ (S_{C1},S_{C2}) \in E_G|_{S \times S}: &&c'(S_{C1},S_{C2}) = \!\!\!\!\!\!\! \sum_{\begin{smallmatrix} (u,v) \in E_G : \\ u \in S_{C1} \, \land \, v \in S_{C2} \end{smallmatrix}} \!\!\!\!\! c(u,v) \\[4pt]
  &\text{otherwise}: &&c'(u,v) = c(u,v)
\end{align}</math>
# Choose two vertices {{math|''s'', ''t'' ∈ ''X''}} and find a minimum {{math|''s''-''t''}} cut {{math|(''A&prime;'', ''B&prime;'')}} in {{mvar|G'}}.
#:Set <math>A = \Biggl(\bigcup_{S_C \in A' \cap S} \!\!\! S_C \! \Biggr) \cup (A' \cap X),\ </math><math>B = \Biggl(\bigcup_{S_C \in B' \cap S} \!\!\! S_C \! \Biggr) \cup (B' \cap X).</math>
# Set <math>V_T = (V_T \setminus X) \cup \{A \cap X, B \cap X \}.
</math> 
#:For each <math>e = (X, Y) \in  E_T</math> do:
#:#Set <math> e' = (A \cap X,Y)</math> if <math> Y \subset A, </math> otherwise set <math>e' = (B \cap X,Y).</math>
#:#Set <math>E_T = (E_T \setminus \{e\}) \cup \{e'\}.</math>
#:#Set <math>w(e') = w(e).</math> 
#:Set <math>E_T = E_T \cup \{(A \cap X,\ B \cap X) \}.</math>
#:Set <math>w((A \cap X, B \cap X)) = c'(A', B').</math>
#:Go to step 2.
# Replace each <math>\{v\} \in V_T</math> by {{mvar|v}} and each <math>(\{u\},\{v\}) \in E_T</math> by {{math|(''u'', ''v'')}}. Output {{mvar|T}}.

==Analysis==
Using the [[submodular]] property of the capacity function {{mvar|c}}, one has
<math display=block>c(X) + c(Y) \ge c(X \cap Y) + c(X \cup Y).</math>
Then it can be shown that the minimum {{math|''s''-''t''}} cut in {{mvar|G'}} is also a minimum {{math|''s''-''t''}} cut in {{mvar|G}} for any {{math|''s'', ''t'' ∈ ''X''}}.

To show that for all <math>(P,Q) \in E_T,</math> <math>w(P,Q) = \lambda_{pq}</math> for some {{math|''p'' ∈ ''P''}}, {{math|''q'' ∈ ''Q''}} throughout the algorithm, one makes use of the following lemma,
: For any {{mvar|i, j, k}} in {{mvar|V<sub>G</sub>}}, <math>\lambda_{ik} \ge \min(\lambda_{ij}, \lambda_{jk}).</math>

The lemma can be used again repeatedly to show that the output {{mvar|T}} satisfies the properties of a Gomory–Hu Tree.

== Implementations: Sequential and Parallel ==
Gusfield's algorithm can be used to find a Gomory–Hu tree without any vertex contraction in the same [[time complexity|running time-complexity]], which simplifies the implementation of constructing a Gomory–Hu Tree.<ref>{{cite journal
 | doi = 10.1137/0219009
 | last = Gusfield | first = Dan
 | title = Very Simple Methods for All Pairs Network Flow Analysis
 | journal = SIAM J. Comput.
 | volume = 19
 | issue = 1
 | pages = 143–155
 | year = 1990
}}</ref>

[[Andrew V. Goldberg]] and K. Tsioutsiouliklis implemented the Gomory-Hu algorithm and Gusfield algorithm, and performed an experimental evaluation and comparison.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Goldberg|first=A. V.|author2=Tsioutsiouliklis, K.|title=Cut Tree Algorithms: An Experimental Study|journal=Journal of Algorithms|year=2001|volume=38|issue=1|pages=51–83|doi=10.1006/jagm.2000.1136 }}</ref>

Cohen et al. report results on two parallel implementations of Gusfield's algorithm using OpenMP and MPI, respectively.<ref>{{cite conference
 | last1 = Cohen | first1 = Jaime
 | last2 = Rodrigues | first2 = Luiz A.
 | last3 = Silva | first3 = Fabiano
 | last4 = Carmo | first4 = Renato
 | last5 = Guedes | first5 = André Luiz Pires
 | last6 = Duarte | first6 = Jr., Elias P.
 | editor1-last = Xiang | editor1-first = Yang
 | editor2-last = Cuzzocrea | editor2-first = Alfredo
 | editor3-last = Hobbs | editor3-first = Michael
 | editor4-last = Zhou | editor4-first = Wanlei
 | contribution = Parallel implementations of Gusfield's cut tree algorithm
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-24650-0_22
 | pages = 258–269
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science
 | title = Algorithms and Architectures for Parallel Processing – 11th International Conference, ICA3PP, Melbourne, Australia, October 24–26, 2011, Proceedings, Part I
 | volume = 7016
 | year = 2011| isbn = 978-3-642-24649-4
 }}</ref>

==Related concepts==
In [[planar graph]]s, the Gomory–Hu tree is dual to the minimum weight [[cycle basis]], in the sense that the cuts of the Gomory–Hu tree are dual to a collection of cycles in the [[dual graph]] that form a minimum-weight cycle basis.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Hartvigsen | first1 = D.
 | last2 = Mardon | first2 = R.
 | doi = 10.1137/S0895480190177042
 | issue = 3
 | journal = SIAM J. Discrete Math.
 | pages = 403–418
 | title = The all-pairs min cut problem and the minimum cycle basis problem on planar graphs
 | volume = 7
 | year = 1994}}.</ref>
